chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
He prays upon the funeral, the person closest to it, or he instructs the one he likes.

key_terms.أَوْلَى النَّاسِ بِهَا: The person closest to the deceased (in terms of kinship or right)

ai.seo_question: Who is entitled to lead the funeral prayer according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the hierarchy for leading the funeral prayer, prioritizing the closest kin (awlā) while granting the authority to appoint a substitute, reflecting the Shia emphasis on familial rights in ritual practice. It underscores the flexibility within the juristic framework, allowing the leader to designate a preferred individual if the closest relative is unavailable or chooses not to lead, thereby ensuring the communal obligation is fulfilled efficiently.
